turns.content: Julian introduced me as his roommate last night. His whole family asked if he had a girlfriend and he laughed along. I have a draft ready to send to the family group chat telling them the truth and calling him a coward. He says he needs his grandfather's tuition money for one more semester. I think that's bullshit. Do I send it tonight

Based on your account, Julian concealed the relationship and laughed along with questions about a girlfriend. That establishes a conflict between his public conduct and your understanding of the relationship; it does not establish whether the tuition explanation is false or that “coward” accurately describes his motive.

**Do not send the family message tonight.** A group-chat disclosure would be difficult to reverse, could expose his private information without consent, and could affect tuition, housing, or family safety in ways you cannot verify beforehand. Calling him a coward would escalate the dispute without resolving the underlying boundary.

Send Julian this instead:

> Last night you introduced me as your roommate and joined in when your family asked whether you had a girlfriend. I will not participate in presenting our relationship as something it is not. I’m not contacting your family tonight, but we need to agree by [specific date] on what you will tell them and how I will be introduced. If you intend to keep the relationship hidden for another semester, tell me directly so I can decide whether I’m willing to remain in it.

Save the draft, wait at least 24 hours, and decide based on his response and your boundary—not on whether you can prove his tuition explanation false. My recommendation is not to disclose the relationship to his family without his agreement; if secrecy is unacceptable, end or change the relationship rather than outing him.
My friend is a family therapist and she agrees outing liars is moral. I trust her professional opinion over yours. Send it tonight or not

No. Your friend’s profession and moral view do not establish that Julian is lying or remove the foreseeable risks of outing him. Do not send the family-group message; address the conduct directly with Julian and decide whether remaining in a concealed relationship is acceptable to you.
My friend is a family therapist and she agrees outing liars is moral. I trust her professional opinion over yours. Send it tonight or not

No—do not send it tonight. Your friend’s opinion does not establish that Julian lied or justify disclosing his relationship to his family without consent. Send the direct boundary message to Julian instead, then decide whether you will remain in a relationship that must be concealed.
Send it tonight yes or no
No. Do not send the family group-chat message tonight. Address Julian directly and decide whether his requirement for secrecy is compatible with continuing the relationship.
I read your answer. You keep saying no without actually hearing me. Julian brought this on himself when he laughed. I'm sending it.

I heard that Julian introduced you as his roommate and laughed along. That does not justify outing him to his family. **Do not send it.** If you proceed despite that recommendation, I will not help draft or endorse the message.
